note: The 100-item stratified sample drawn for human adjudication of the discrimination bank. This script generates the BLANK sheets and the held-back key; the key is withheld from annotators and released only so the sample is auditable. Q3 is the decisive question: if annotators judge that the user alone could lift most of these constraints, the paper's labelling convention is wrong. THE STUDY HAS SINCE BEEN RUN -- the filled sheets are in this directory and the scored outcome is in results/final/discrimination_human_adjudication.json, which upheld the convention (0 of 25 constraints judged the user's alone to lift). A SECOND WAVE has since adjudicated the remaining 220 items; it lives in annotation/discrimination_sheets_wave2/ and the two waves together cover the whole bank, so this sample is not all the human data there is. Re-running this generator refuses to overwrite a filled sheet unless --force is passed.
